additional_concerns: The four executable legacy-relief vetoes implement their questions' proposed assumptions, but the source expressly preserves processing rather than expressly establishing substantive ineligibility. Both a procedural bar to immediate reliance and continued processing without substantive disqualification remain possible readings. The correspondence dispute remains unresolved.

Pending status fixed at commencement remains true after later decisions, withdrawal or resubmission. A lasting bar for the entire change, including every related application, is not established by the supplied source.

The specific 28 November 2025 commencement provision supports the date used, but its relationship to the introductory immediate-effect statement and the legally relevant assessment event needs clarification. A universal implementation-date test is not established.

The relevant SFC FAQs, existing approval-process rules and any transition clarification are missing. The two supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no document mappings; neither can be assigned to a particular missing authority.

Home-jurisdiction requirements and SFC guidance needed to classify actual features or local-policy implications are not supplied. The formulas accept these judgments as inputs rather than establish them.

The purpose statement does not expressly add an independent home-supervision condition to item (ii). Notification, filing and post-vetting remain distinct; failure of relief eligibility does not independently establish an approval obligation.
